SUMMARY: Track B capstone: task manager on Amazon EKS with GitOps
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to run the task-manager app on EKS with GitOps, synced secrets, one ingress and autoscaling so that I complete the Track B capstone.
DESCRIPTION: Learner backlog for Track B (shared foundation M1 + M9–M16), following the content packs and the Track B capstone brief. All rows start To Do; update STATUS in your own copy as you go. Every AWS resource is created by Terraform; each session ends with terraform destroy in reverse order, checking the load balancer is gone before the cluster.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- All 20 Track B capstone requirements met
- Documentation Gate evidence complete in `docs/capstone/`
- Live 30-minute defense passed (75%+ and gate met)

SUMMARY: Set up tools, AWS access and the infra/ folder
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want my tools, AWS identity and Terraform backend settings ready so that every later stack starts from the same setup.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab steps 1–2). Install/check Terraform 1.11+, AWS CLI v2, Docker buildx, git, curl, jq. Confirm `aws sts get-caller-identity` and region `ap-southeast-1`. In your gitlab.com project add `infra/backend.hcl` (your state bucket, `use_lockfile = true`, `encrypt = true`) and `infra/env.sh` (`TF_VAR_learner_id`, `TF_VAR_state_bucket`).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `aws sts get-caller-identity` shows the sandbox account
- `aws configure get region` prints `ap-southeast-1`
- `infra/backend.hcl` and `infra/env.sh` are committed, with no secrets in either

SUMMARY: Pin Terraform and create the ECR repositories
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want pinned providers and two ECR repositories so that everyone gets the same behavior and my images have a home.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab steps 3–4). In `infra/10-foundation`: `versions.tf` (required_version >= 1.11, aws 6.66.0, random 3.9.1, S3 backend key `dcta/10-foundation.tfstate`, standard `default_tags`), `variables.tf` (region, learner_id, learner_cidr with /32 validation), `ecr.tf` (`dcta-frontend`, `dcta-backend`, IMMUTABLE tags, lifecycle: expire untagged after 1 day, keep last 2 tagged).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Provider versions are exact and `.terraform.lock.hcl` is committed
- `terraform -chdir=infra/10-foundation apply` creates both repositories
- Tags are immutable and the lifecycle policy keeps the last 2 images

SUMMARY: Store the DB password without it ever touching state
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the database password generated straight into Secrets Manager so that it never appears in Git or any Terraform state file.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 5). `secrets.tf` in 10-foundation: `ephemeral "random_password"`, `aws_secretsmanager_secret` `dcta/db/credentials` (recovery window 0), `aws_secretsmanager_secret_version` with `secret_string_wo` (username `taskadmin` + password) and `secret_string_wo_version`, plus SSM parameter `/dcta/db/name` = `taskdb`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `terraform state show aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db` shows no secret string
- No password in Git history
- `/dcta/db/name` exists in Parameter Store

SUMMARY: Prepare the app for AWS (TLS, production frontend, seed)
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the reference app ready to run on AWS so that it connects to RDS over TLS, fits a small container and gets a fresh schema every session.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 7). (a) Backend `server.js`: `ssl` option driven by `DB_SSL_CA_PATH`; backend Dockerfile adds the RDS ap-southeast-1 CA bundle. (b) Frontend: multi-stage Dockerfile (node build → `nginx:1.30-alpine`), `REACT_APP_API_URL=/api`, remove the `location /api/` block from `nginx.conf`. (c) `app/database/seed.sql`: re-runnable schema + 3 sample tasks.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Local `docker compose up` still works (DB_SSL_CA_PATH unset)
- Frontend image serves the React build from nginx on port 80
- Running `seed.sql` twice adds no duplicate rows

SUMMARY: Build and push amd64 images tagged with the Git SHA
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want both images in ECR, built for amd64 and tagged with my commit, so that AWS can run them and I always know which code is live.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 (Hands-on lab step 8). Log Docker in with `aws ecr get-login-password`, then `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 -t <registry>/dcta-<app>:<short-sha> --push` for backend and frontend.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `aws ecr describe-images` lists the short commit SHA for both repositories
- Images are linux/amd64
- No `latest` tag is used

SUMMARY: Write the VPC with no NAT Gateway
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want a 2-AZ VPC with public and private subnets so that containers can reach ECR directly and the database stays private.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise item 1. In 10-foundation: VPC across `ap-southeast-1a`/`1b`, 2 public + 2 private subnets, Internet Gateway, public route table, no NAT Gateway, `map_public_ip_on_launch = true` on the public subnets.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- 4 subnets, 2 per AZ
- `describe-nat-gateways` count is 0
- Public subnets assign public IPs on launch

SUMMARY: Chain the security groups and publish the foundation outputs
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want security groups that point at each other and a stable outputs contract so that only my app can reach the database and later stacks can read the foundation.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise items 2–3. `dcta-alb-sg`, `dcta-app-sg`, `dcta-rds-sg`: internet ingress only from `var.learner_cidr`; RDS 5432 only from `dcta-app-sg`; any 0.0.0.0/0 egress carries a `# justification:` comment. Outputs exactly: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, alb_sg_id, app_sg_id, rds_sg_id, ecr_repository_urls, db_secret_arn, db_name_parameter_arn.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `dcta-rds-sg` ingress references `dcta-app-sg`, with no IP ranges
- No internet-facing 0.0.0.0/0 ingress
- All 9 outputs exist with the exact names

SUMMARY: Create the ephemeral database stack
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want RDS in its own stack that I create and destroy every session so that it only exists while I work and is never reachable from the internet.
DESCRIPTION: Shared foundation, M1 Lab exercise items 4–5. `infra/20-data` (key `dcta/20-data.tfstate`): `terraform_remote_state` of 10-foundation, DB subnet group on the private subnets, `aws_db_instance` `dcta-postgres` (PostgreSQL 17, db.t4g.micro, `password_wo` from the ephemeral secret, not public, no final snapshot), SSM `/dcta/db/host`; output `db_host_parameter_arn`. Destroy and re-apply it with no manual steps.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- RDS is available, `PubliclyAccessible: false`, in the private subnets
- `/dcta/db/host` holds the RDS address
- Destroy + re-apply works with no manual steps
- Failure path: `nc` from your laptop to RDS on 5432 fails

SUMMARY: Create the Track B cluster stack skeleton
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the cluster stack and my Kubernetes tools ready so that I can create and reach an EKS cluster each session.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M9 (Hands-on lab steps 1–4). Install/check kubectl (within one minor of 1.36), helm 3, eksctl (read-only use). `infra/40-track-b-cluster`: versions (aws 6.66.0, key `dcta/40-track-b-cluster.tfstate`), variables, `terraform_remote_state` of 10-foundation. Learn the Track B session commands.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Tools installed
- Stack reads the VPC from 10-foundation outputs

SUMMARY: Create the EKS cluster with prefix delegation
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want an EKS cluster reachable only from my IP so that I have a secure, low-cost Kubernetes control plane.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M9 Lab exercise items 1–3. `terraform-aws-modules/eks/aws` 21.26.0: cluster `dcta-eks`, Kubernetes 1.36, nodes in public subnets, control plane ENIs in private subnets, endpoint public only to `var.learner_cidr`, cluster-creator admin via access entry, control-plane logging and the module log group off, add-ons CoreDNS / kube-proxy / VPC CNI (VPC CNI before compute with ENABLE_PREFIX_DELEGATION=true).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `kubectl get nodes` works from your laptop
- API endpoint only accepts your /32
- No control-plane log group is created

SUMMARY: Add the single Spot node and check it
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one Spot worker node that can run the whole stack and reach RDS so that my pods have somewhere to run.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M9 Lab exercise items 4–6. Managed node group: AL2023 x86_64, capacity_type SPOT, t3.medium + t3a.medium, 1/1/1, `dcta-app-sg` attached. Outputs cluster_name, oidc_provider_arn, oidc_provider.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- One node, SPOT, t3.medium/t3a.medium, in a public subnet
- Node pod capacity is 110
- NAT Gateway count is 0
- `pg_isready` from a pod reports accepting connections

SUMMARY: Create the IRSA role for External Secrets and test it
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one IAM role that only the External Secrets ServiceAccount can use so that pods get AWS access with no keys.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M10 Lab exercise items 7–8 + failure proof. `dcta-eso-irsa`: trust StringEquals on sub `system:serviceaccount:external-secrets:external-secrets` and aud `sts.amazonaws.com`; permissions GetSecretValue + DescribeSecret on the DB secret, GetParameter on `/dcta/db/host` and `/dcta/db/name`; output `eso_irsa_role_arn`. Test with an annotated ServiceAccount, then delete the test namespace.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Allowed pod shows `assumed-role/dcta-eso-irsa` and reads the DB secret name
- Failure path: allowed pod is denied another secret
- Failure path: a `default` ServiceAccount pod can't read the DB secret

SUMMARY: Create the platform stack and install External Secrets
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want External Secrets installed by Terraform so that the cluster can sync the DB settings from AWS.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M11 (Hands-on lab steps 1–3). `infra/41-track-b-platform`: aws 6.66.0 + helm 3.3.0 (v3 attribute syntax), `aws_eks_cluster` data source, `terraform_remote_state` of the cluster stack, `helm_release` external-secrets 2.11.0 with the IRSA role annotation.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `helm list -n external-secrets` shows chart 2.11.0
- ESO ServiceAccount carries the `dcta-eso-irsa` role ARN

SUMMARY: Sync the DB settings with ExternalSecrets
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want Kubernetes Secrets created from AWS so that no password is ever written in my repository.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M11 Lab exercise items 1–2 + failure proof. `deploy/platform/cluster-secret-stores.yaml` (Secrets Manager + Parameter Store stores, no auth block) and `deploy/apps/task-app/external-secrets.yaml` (task-app namespace; `db-credentials` with DB_USER/DB_PASSWORD, `db-config` with DB_HOST/DB_NAME).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Both stores Ready; both ExternalSecrets SecretSynced
- Secrets hold exactly the 4 keys
- `git grep` finds no DB password
- Failure path: pointing at a forbidden secret reports access denied and leaves the existing Secret unchanged

SUMMARY: Move the chart and add the seed Job
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want my local-phase chart in the repo with a seed hook so that every install gets a ready database.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M12 (Hands-on lab steps 1–2). Move the `task-app` chart to `deploy/charts/task-app/`, copy `seed.sql` into `files/`, add the `db-seed` ConfigMap + post-install/post-upgrade Job reading `db-credentials` and `db-config`; `seed.enabled: false` in values.yaml.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- `helm lint` passes
- `helm template` renders the seed ConfigMap and Job only when seed is enabled

SUMMARY: Deploy the app to EKS with values-eks.yaml
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one chart that deploys to both Minikube and EKS so that the same app runs in the cloud with no in-cluster database.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M12 Lab exercise items 3–5 + failure proof. `values-eks.yaml` + template changes: no PostgreSQL pod, ECR SHA-tagged images, frontend on port 80, backend envFrom the two ESO Secrets plus PORT/DB_PORT/DB_SSL_CA_PATH, requests + memory limits + `/health` probes, seed enabled. Install with `helm upgrade --install`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Seed Job completes; upgrading again adds no rows
- Via port-forward the backend lists and creates tasks in RDS
- Failure path: a bad image tag is diagnosed from pod events while the old pod keeps serving

SUMMARY: Install the NGINX Ingress Controller behind one NLB
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want one load balancer in front of the cluster, open only to me, so that the app has a single public address.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M13 Lab exercise item 1. `helm_release` nginx-ingress 2.7.3 (helm.nginx.com/stable), namespace `nginx-ingress`: Service type LoadBalancer with the NLB annotation, `loadBalancerSourceRanges = [var.learner_cidr]`, ingress class `nginx`, host-less Ingresses allowed, `wait = true`, timeout ≥ 900, small requests.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Exactly one load balancer, of type network
- Only your /32 can reach it

SUMMARY: Route the app through the Ingress
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want an Ingress that sends /api to the backend and / to the frontend so that the app works in a browser.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M13 Lab exercise items 2–3 + failure proof. `templates/ingress.yaml` (enabled from values-eks.yaml): class nginx, no host, `/api` → backend:3000, `/` → frontend:80.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- The app works in a browser via the NLB address
- Failure path: with the backend at 0 replicas, `/api/tasks` returns a 5xx while `/` still works

SUMMARY: Install Argo CD and connect the repo
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want Argo CD installed by Terraform with read-only access to my repo so that Git can drive the cluster.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M14 Lab exercise items 4–5. `helm_release` argo-cd 10.9.2, namespace `argocd`, Dex and notifications off, `wait = true`; UI via port-forward only. Create a read-only GitLab deploy token and the Argo CD repository Secret from your shell each session.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Argo CD pods healthy; no public Service for its UI
- Deploy token is read-only and never in Git

SUMMARY: Create the Argo CD Applications
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want everything in the cluster managed by Argo CD Applications so that the cluster always matches Git.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M14 Lab exercise item 6. `deploy/argocd/`: `platform` (deploy/platform), `task-app-secrets` (deploy/apps/task-app), `task-app` (chart + values-eks.yaml, namespace task-app) — all automated sync, prune, selfHeal, CreateNamespace=true. Remove any hand-installed Helm release first.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: - All three Applications Synced and Healthy

SUMMARY: Prove GitOps, self-heal and revert
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to see Git changes, manual drift and bad commits handled by Argo CD so that I can rely on GitOps at the defense.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M14 Lab exercise item 7 + failure proofs. Push a visible change and watch OutOfSync → Synced. Delete the backend Deployment by hand. Push a non-existent image tag, then `git revert`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- A commit alone changes the running app
- Failure path: a deleted Deployment is recreated by self-heal
- Failure path: a bad commit goes Degraded while the old pod keeps serving, then Healthy after `git revert`

SUMMARY: Deploy metrics-server with Argo CD
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want live CPU and memory numbers in the cluster so that the HPA can make scaling decisions.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M15 (Hands-on lab step 1). `deploy/argocd/metrics-server.yaml`: chart metrics-server 3.14.0 into kube-system, small requests, automated sync.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- metrics-server Application Synced and Healthy
- `kubectl top pods` works

SUMMARY: Deploy Prometheus and Grafana with Argo CD
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want cluster monitoring deployed the GitOps way so that I can watch the app scale in Grafana.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M15 Lab exercise items 1, 2 and 4. `grafana-admin` Secret created from your shell; Application for kube-prometheus-stack 91.8.1 (ServerSideApply=true, Alertmanager off, EKS-managed control-plane targets off, 6h retention, small requests, Grafana admin from the Secret, Ingress host `grafana.dcta.test`). Point `grafana.dcta.test` at the NLB in your browser's hosts file.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Application Synced and Healthy
- Grafana reachable at `grafana.dcta.test` on the same NLB
- No password in Git

SUMMARY: Add the HPA and prove it under load
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want the backend to scale from 1 to 3 pods at 70% CPU so that it handles load by itself.
DESCRIPTION: Track B, M15 Lab exercise items 3 and 5 + failure proof. `templates/hpa.yaml` (autoscaling/v2, 1–3, 70% CPU), backend CPU request, Deployment leaves out `replicas` when autoscaling is on. 5-minute `ab` load test; Grafana query `kube_horizontalpodautoscaler_status_current_replicas`.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- HPA reaches 3 replicas under load and returns to 1
- HPA events and a Grafana screenshot saved
- Failure path: without a CPU request the HPA shows <unknown> with the reason, fixed by `git revert`

SUMMARY: Rebuild from scratch and write the decision matrix
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to rebuild the whole environment from scratch and record the key choices in my build so that I know my repository alone recreates everything and I can defend my design.
DESCRIPTION: Track B capstone, integration day (Week 6 Day 4). Destroy every session stack, then apply 20-data, 40-track-b-cluster and 41-track-b-platform, recreate the session Secrets from your shell (deploy token, grafana-admin) and run `kubectl apply -f deploy/argocd/` — everything must come back from Git alone. Then write `docs/capstone/decision-matrix.md` with at least 5 rows: Decision | What I chose | Alternative I considered | Trade-off | Evidence from my build (e.g. pod credentials, password delivery, traffic entry, deployment model, node sizing, HPA settings, teardown order).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- After the rebuild from scratch, every Application is Synced and Healthy with no manual kubectl apply or helm install of app resources
- The app, Grafana and the HPA work again after the rebuild
- Decision matrix has at least 5 rows, each with real evidence from your build

SUMMARY: Complete the capstone documentation
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want all my evidence in one place so that I pass the Documentation Gate.
DESCRIPTION: Track B capstone Documentation section. In `docs/capstone/`: apply/destroy output for 10-foundation, 20-data, 40-track-b-cluster, 41-track-b-platform; failed `nc`, NAT count, node pod capacity; IRSA test logs; ESO status, forbidden-secret status and `git grep`; routing and backend-at-0 tests; Argo CD commit, self-heal and revert evidence; HPA events and Grafana screenshot; teardown proof; own-words explanation of the daily apply/destroy order.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Every evidence item in the capstone spec's Documentation list is present and real
- Own-words explanation of the apply/destroy order is included

SUMMARY: Rehearse the 30-minute defense
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want a practiced run-through so that the live defense fits in 30 minutes.
DESCRIPTION: Track B capstone (Day 10 prep). Follow the rubric agenda: session start and everything Synced, commit → sync + self-heal, load test → HPA → Grafana, decision matrix, teardown with the NLB check, then Q&A and a live destructive test. Prepare answers to the rubric's "why" questions.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- A full run-through fits in 30 minutes, including Q&A time
- You can answer each of the rubric's Track B "why" questions

SUMMARY: Deliver the live 30-minute defense and tear everything down
USER_STORY: As a learner, I want to demonstrate the whole system live and leave nothing running so that I complete Track B.
DESCRIPTION: Track B capstone, M16. Live 30-minute defense per the rubric, then destroy 41-track-b-platform, confirm `describe-load-balancers` returns 0, destroy 40-track-b-cluster and 20-data. Last day only: destroy 10-foundation.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Defense completed within 30 minutes
- NLB confirmed gone before the cluster was destroyed
- No load balancer or NAT Gateway remains; last day: 10-foundation destroyed
